name: CUDA C++
comment: CUDA is C++ plus a layer of its own: the placement qualifiers, the launch brackets, and the built-in types nvcc's headers declare. Everything else is C++, so the last pattern hands the text to the built-in `source.cpp` grammar rather than restating it — one grammar for C++ and one small file for the layer on top.

patterns.comment: The placement qualifiers — a specifier the language does not have. `__launch_bounds__(…)` and its family are written with arguments; the name is what carries the meaning.
patterns.name: storage.modifier.qualifier.cuda

patterns.comment: The launch brackets: `k<<<grid, block>>>(args)`. They are not C++ at all, and giving them their own colour is what makes a launch readable next to the shifts it lexes as.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.launch.cuda

patterns.comment: The built-in variables and vector types — declared by `cuda_runtime.h` and `vector_types.h`, so they belong to the toolkit rather than to the grammar; highlighted because a reader meets them before reading either header.
patterns.name: support.variable.builtin.cuda
